D007-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for about the past seven months. At first, I just felt empty—like nothing mattered. I stopped caring about work, even though I’ve driven a cab for over fifteen years. Getting out of bed became a fight. I sleep six or seven hours, but wake up exhausted, like I’ve been up all night. My hands won’t stay still—I’m always picking at my fingers or pacing in the cab when I’m on break. It’s like my body’s restless even when my mind’s numb.

Then the other stuff started. I became convinced my ex was cheating on me, even after our divorce. I *know* we’re split, but I keep seeing her—sometimes in the back seat, sometimes standing on the sidewalk, watching me. I *see* her, clear as anything, but when I check, she’s gone. I try to explain things to dispatch or passengers, but they don’t get it. I find myself going off on tangents, talking about things that aren’t related, because my thoughts just… drift.

The low mood and the visions, the jealousy—it’s been happening together since it all began. Honestly, I’ve felt this way most days for months. The dark thoughts and the seeing things—they overlap so much, I can’t tell where one ends and the other starts.
D007-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling overwhelming sadness for the past seven months—like a heavy fog I can’t shake. I can’t fall asleep most nights, even when I’m exhausted, and when I do, I wake up feeling like my body is made of concrete. Moving is so slow, I see it frustrates my clients at work. I used to be good at my job—connecting with people, closing policies—but now I just stay home, avoid calls, even from my ex-husband.  

For about six months now, I’ve also been feeling bugs crawling under my skin, something scratching me when nothing’s there. I know it sounds odd, but it's real to me. And lately... I’ve had this certainty that the world is ending—like the sun is going to implode soon and we’re all just delaying the inevitable. I call it “sol collapse,” just between me and you—it’s what I’ve started writing in my journal.  

What scares me more is that even when I don’t feel completely hopeless, those visions and the crawling? They stay. For weeks at a time, the thoughts about the end persist *even when I’m not depressed*. That’s why I came—if the darkness lifts a little, but the delusions don’t, then it’s not just depression, is it?
D007-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h003.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—things started slipping at work, and I couldn’t keep up with prescriptions like I used to. I feel heavy all the time, like I’m moving through mud. My speech slows down, even when I’m trying to answer simple questions. I don’t enjoy anything anymore—not my job, not walking my dog, not even talking to friends. I wake up after eight hours and still feel exhausted, like I’ve been running all night.  

But it’s not just the sadness. For the past six months, I’ve known—*known*—that the pharmacist across town is in love with me. He doesn’t say it, but I can feel it. He sends signs through the way he arranges his window displays. And I keep smelling cigarette smoke, even when no one’s around—like something’s burning in the walls. Sometimes I catch myself rhyming when I talk, like, “I file the files with healing smiles”—it just comes out that way.  

The truth is, the lows have been here almost the whole time. Even when the mania or the smells flare up, the depression never really leaves. It’s been like this for most of the last half-year. I think the voices and the beliefs would’ve come even if I weren’t depressed—but the sadness? It’s been constant.
D007-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been a nurse in the ER for three years, and up until about seven months ago, I was handling the chaos just fine. Lately, though, I can’t stop crying at work—little things set me off, and I’ve lost interest in everything, even things I used to love, like painting and seeing my friends. I haven’t been sleeping right either—I wake up two or three times every night and can’t go back to sleep, just lying there, restless, pacing my room, picking at my skin until it bleeds.  

For the past six months, I’ve also been convinced something’s poisoning my blood—like my organs are rotting. I smell this awful metallic stench, like burnt hair or chemicals, but no one else does. I told the doctor last month, and she checked my labs—everything was normal. I’ve been jumping from one thought to the next during handoffs at work—my speech gets all tangled, and I can see the confusion on my colleagues’ faces.  

The mood stuff has been there almost the whole time, really. But there were two weeks last fall, after a panic attack at work, when I wasn’t as depressed, but I still smelled the odor and believed my blood was toxic. That’s when they sent me here.
D007-D005_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h005.question:
I’ve been really struggling for about the last seven months. I used to find peace in working with metal—focusing on the sparks, the heat—but now I can’t even make it through a shift without feeling completely drained. I’ve been sleeping up to 12 hours a day, sometimes napping right after breakfast, but I still feel slow, like my body’s dragging behind me. I don’t enjoy anything anymore—not my wife, not my truck, not even grilling, which I used to love.

But it’s not just the depression. For the past six months, I’ve known—*known*—that a news anchor from the local station, this woman named Claire, she’s in love with me. I don’t know her personally, but she winks at me through the screen, sends subtle signs in her posture. I even see her sometimes, standing outside the garage during my break, or in the aisle at the grocery store, just watching. She’s trying to tell me something, I can feel it.

I’ve had trouble talking clearly too—I jump from topic to topic, and my wife says I lose her. There was a two-week stretch last month when I wasn't as down, but I *still* saw Claire, still knew she was trying to reach me. Even when I'm not as sad, those thoughts and visions don't go away.
D007-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h006.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—maybe closer to 16 months. At first, I thought it was just grief after losing my husband, but it’s gone so far beyond that. I don’t feel anything inside—just empty, like there’s a hollow space where my heart used to be. I used to love volunteering at the church kitchen, but now I can’t even stand the thought of food. I barely eat; nothing tastes right anyway. In fact, out of nowhere, I’ll taste something metallic, like blood, even when I’m just drinking water. The doctors can’t find anything wrong, but I know what I’m tasting.

I’ve started believing things… awful things. Like the food I used to serve was poisoned, and now everyone who ate it is sick or dying because of me. I know it doesn’t make sense, but the guilt is crushing—it feels real. Sometimes I think the world is ending, that it’s already fallen apart and I’m just too blind to see it. My thoughts jump around—my daughter’s birthday, then the war on TV, then how I ruined the soup last Tuesday—it’s all connected, but I can’t explain how.

The worst part? Even when I’m not feeling so down, the voices and tastes and fears don’t go away. They’ve been there, steady, for weeks on end, even when my mood lifts slightly. But honestly, the sadness has been there much longer, and it’s what drains me the most.
D007-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—about sixteen months now—and things have just gotten worse. At work, I started noticing cameras everywhere, even in places they shouldn’t be. I know it sounds strange, but I’m certain my bosses are monitoring me, feeding false data into the system to frame me for audits I didn’t sabotage. Sometimes, I see figures standing in the server room doorway, but when I approach, no one’s there.  

At the same time, I’ve felt this crushing emptiness, like I’m emotionally numb. I lost over twenty pounds because I just couldn’t eat—food meant nothing. I stopped seeing friends, stopped answering calls. I even believe I caused my cousin’s car accident last year, that my negative energy somehow made it happen, even though I wasn’t anywhere near.  

And here’s the thing—these dark thoughts, the guilt, the emptiness—it’s been there most of the time, almost from the beginning. I’ve had stretches where the paranoia and the visions stayed, even when I wasn’t feeling depressed. But the sadness? That’s been with me far longer than not. It’s like the depression has been running the show, with psychosis tagging along. I can’t keep up at work anymore—I just sit at my desk, exhausted, watching shadows move.
D007-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—about sixteen months, I’d say. At first, it was hard to tell what was going on. As a news anchor, I’m used to being sharp, on top of things, but I started feeling… off. I’d be on air and swear the teleprompter messages had hidden meanings just for me—like they were sending me signals only I could understand. Even random comments from coworkers felt like secret messages directed at me.  

Then, I began feeling this crawling sensation on my skin, like bugs moving underneath, but no one else could see anything. It still happens. My thoughts? They jump around—today I’ll be talking about a script, then suddenly I’m thinking about guilt, how I must’ve caused that plane crash last winter, even though I wasn’t even near it. I know that sounds irrational, but the guilt feels real, crushing.  

I’ve lost all interest in things I used to love—makeup, fashion, even anchoring. I feel empty. I’ve gained over twenty pounds recently, just from not caring. And honestly, this low mood? It’s been here most of the time, longer than the breaks between my strange thoughts and sensations. In fact, there were only a few weeks last spring when I wasn’t depressed, but the delusions and hallucinations still crept in.
D007-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h009.question:
I’ve been feeling completely off for over a year now—maybe closer to fifteen months. At work, I used to take pride in keeping things running smoothly on the floor, but now I can’t focus. My mind jumps around—like one second I’m thinking about safety logs, the next I’m convinced the foreman is part of a conspiracy to frame me. I know it sounds crazy, but I *feel* them—bugs crawling under my skin, especially at night. No one’s touching me, but the sensation won’t quit.

About a year ago, I stopped caring about things I used to love—weekend grilling, tinkering with my truck. I’ve gained about twenty pounds since then. I can’t shake this guilt, like I caused my sister’s car accident last winter, even though I wasn’t anywhere near it. I barely talk to my wife now; I just feel empty. What’s worse is that for over two months straight, I was hearing things and deeply paranoid, even when I wasn’t feeling depressed. That time stands out because the thoughts were loud, but the sadness wasn’t there—I was just trapped in the fear. The depression’s been here far longer than the breaks, though. It’s been the main thing, really.
D007-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe a year and a half now. At first, I’d feel this deep emptiness, like nothing mattered, not even finishing projects that used to make me proud. I stopped caring about my work, even though I used to take such pride in designing gardens. My appetite shot up; I’d eat even when I wasn’t hungry, just to fill *something*. I kept thinking, *What’s the point? I’m worthless anyway.*  

But then, things got weird. I started smelling burning leaves everywhere—on the bus, in my apartment—no matter where I went. I knew it wasn’t real, but I couldn’t shake it. People walking by would mutter or glance, and I just *knew* they were talking about me, sending signals. Once, a client said “pruning season” and I went on for ten minutes about storm warnings and survival, totally off track.  

It’s been like this for so long—most of the time, I’m crushed by sadness *and* caught in these thoughts and smells. There were a few stretches—maybe three weeks at a time—where the sadness lifted a little, but the voices and smells stayed. Honestly, the low mood has been here way longer than not. I can’t keep working like this.
D007-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—ever since I started hearing voices. At first, it was whispers during quiet moments, but now they’re constant, telling me the world is ending, that everything is pointless and already destroyed. I believe it—deep down, I know it sounds crazy, but I feel it’s true. I’ve stopped going out, stopped calling friends. What’s the point? Everyone I care about is going to vanish anyway.

I used to love my job in HR, but now I can’t sit still during meetings—my hands won’t stop shaking, I pace, pick at my skin. I feel guilty all the time, like I’ve failed everyone. I’ve even thought it would be better if I just weren’t here, though I wouldn’t hurt my family. But some days, the guilt is so heavy, I think I deserve to.

My speech? People tell me I don’t make sense anymore—jumping between thoughts, words jumbled. I don’t even realize it’s happening. And I’ve developed these odd habits, tapping my fingers in a certain way, like a ritual.

The low mood, the guilt, the voices, the delusions—they’ve been there together from the start, almost every day. I’ve felt this way more than not since it began. The voices were there even when I wasn’t depressed, but the sadness has been with me through most of this.
D007-D005_h011.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h012.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—ever since that shift at the precinct when I first smelled smoke that no one else did. It’s always burning rubber or rotting meat, but there’s nothing there. I know that sounds crazy, but I *know* the world’s ending. It’s all collapsing… and I’m just waiting for it to happen. Sometimes I try to explain it, but my words get tangled—like my thoughts won’t line up. I’ll catch myself repeating the same motion, like tapping my fingers or pacing the same spot, over and over. And honestly, I don’t even care to talk much anymore.

I haven’t felt anything real in months. My wife tries, but I can’t enjoy anything—not my job, not even being with her. I move like I’m underwater. I feel like a ghost. Worst of all, I’ve planned how I’d do it—gun in the garage, after shift, when she’s asleep. But here’s the thing—those voices and smells? They were still there *before* I started feeling this depressed, and they stayed after the worst of the sadness hit. The truth is, I’ve felt this low for most of the last seven months, and the psychosis never really stopped.
D007-D005_h012.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h013.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now. At first, I thought it was stress—work slowed down, and I just didn’t care anymore, even about projects I used to love. I stopped answering client calls, canceled meetings. My husband says I’ve changed. I feel so heavy, like every move takes effort. Walking to the kitchen feels exhausting. I look in the mirror and think something’s wrong inside me—like my organs are rotting, even though the doctors say tests are normal. Sometimes I feel bugs crawling under my skin, and I scratch until it bleeds, but there’s nothing there.  

I catch myself repeating motions—pacing the same path in the living room, adjusting the blinds over and over. My thoughts? They slip. I’ll say things like “I light the night with flighty fright,” just because the words click. I don’t want to see anyone. Friends stopped calling.  

The worst part is the emptiness. I used to take pride in my designs, now it means nothing. I feel worthless. Sometimes, standing on the balcony, I get this sudden urge to jump—not because I’ve planned it, but the pull is there.  

For at least two weeks, I was extra paranoid and jumbled without feeling deeply depressed—just voices and delusions. But honestly, most of the time, the sadness and the symptoms are both there, together. It’s been like this most of the year.
D007-D005_h013.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h014.question:
I’ve been working nights at the mall for years, but things started changing about seven months ago. I began hearing voices—sometimes they talk to me, telling me I’m chosen, that I can see the future and control events with my mind. I know I’m just a security guard, but I really believe I have a divine mission. I catch myself saying things that rhyme for no reason, like “clock the shock” or “fence the sense,” and I’ll sometimes freeze in one position for a long time—even when my back hurts from standing stiff.

But it’s not just that. I feel slow—like my thoughts are underwater. Talking takes effort. My wife says I don’t show emotions like I used to. I don’t want to see anyone, not even my boys from work. I feel useless, like I’ve never mattered. Some mornings, I think, “Maybe I shouldn’t wake up.” This low mood, the voices, the odd thoughts—they’ve all been here since it started. The truth is, I’ve felt this way most of the time for months. There were maybe a couple of weeks early on where the voices came without the sadness, but nearly every day since has been both—the voices *and* the darkness.
D007-D005_h014.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h015.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now. At first, I stopped caring about my bakery—used to take pride in opening early, arranging the display, chatting with regulars. Now I can’t even bring myself to turn the lights on most days. I move so slowly, like I’m underwater. I’ve thought about ending it all—figured I could take pills after closing, when no one’s around. I don’t want my daughter to find me, so I’ve imagined doing it at the old cottage, on a quiet Tuesday.

But it’s not just the sadness. There’s more. I see my late husband sometimes, standing in the kitchen like he’s still working beside me. Other times, I see strangers watching me from the alley. And I know this might sound strange, but I’m certain that a famous baker from TV—someone I’ve never met—is secretly in love with me, that he’ll come and save me. I’ve written him letters, told him how I feel.

My daughter says I don’t make sense when I talk—like my words get tangled. I laugh sometimes for no reason, like a little girl, and then go silent for hours. I know I’ve changed. But the truth is, the dark mood has been there almost every day since this started. It’s not just the voices and visions—it’s the weight of it all, together, for months and months.
D007-D005_h015.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h016.question:
I’ve been struggling for over eight months—maybe closer to ten now. At first, I thought it was just stress from work; running a bank branch means long hours and constant pressure. But things changed. I started feeling... empty. No joy, no sadness—just this hollow space inside. I lost over 15 pounds without trying. My clothes hang off me. I’m exhausted all the time, even walking to the bathroom feels like a marathon.

Then the nightmares began—vivid, terrifying dreams every night. I’d wake up sweating, heart racing, and sometimes… I’d see shadows in the corner of the room. A figure standing there. Once, I saw my late father at the foot of the bed, just watching. He wasn’t real—I know that now—but it felt real then.

At work, I started thinking people were talking about me. Clients would glance over, and I was sure they were sending me coded messages. My assistant said “good morning,” and I believed she was warning me about surveillance.

The low mood, the fatigue, the nightmares—they’ve been there almost the whole time. But there were weeks, especially earlier, when I was hearing and seeing things even when I wasn’t depressed. That’s when I knew something deeper was wrong.
D007-D005_h016.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h017.question: I’ve been the head nurse on a busy floor for over twenty years, but lately, I can’t keep up. D007-D005_h019.question:
I’ve been struggling for about ten months now—ever since my husband passed. At first, I thought it was just grief, but things got worse. I can’t sleep like I used to; it takes hours just to fall asleep, even when I’m exhausted. I’m tired all the time, no matter how much I rest. Food doesn’t bring comfort—ironically, I’ve been eating more, but I feel nothing, like my heart’s gone numb.

D007-D005_h020.question:

I stopped feeling hungry, lost weight—my wife kept asking if I was sick. I cried sometimes for no reason, which embarrassed me. I even see her in places she couldn’t be—standing at the end of the hall at work, or in my peripheral vision at the grocery store. She’s trying to tell me something, I’m sure of it.

D007-D005_h020.options:

D007-D005_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—almost a year and a half now. Lately, everything feels like it’s screaming at me. People on TV, even strangers in the hallway at school, I know they’re sending me messages. They don’t say it outright, but it’s coded—like when my teacher said “the stars align,” I knew he meant *me*. I started calling that “stargap”—it’s when the universe winks at you, and only I get it. I made that word up.

I can’t sit still. I pace my room at night, wringing my hands, picking at my arms. It’s like my skin’s crawling. I used to love playing guitar, hanging out with friends, even video games—now nothing feels like it matters. I just feel… hollow. I haven’t slept well in forever. I lie down and my mind races—thoughts, images—sometimes I see shadows moving in the corners, like figures watching me. That’s happened even when I wasn’t feeling sad, like last summer, when I was just… out there.

But most of the time, I’m stuck in this heavy sadness. It’s been like this way longer than the times I’m not depressed. I barely go to school anymore. I just can’t.

    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D005_h022.question:
I’ve been here in this room for over a year now—ever since my John passed, though sometimes I still see him whispering to that nurse down the hall, stealing kisses behind the medication cart. They’re always together, I know it. That’s when I start repeating names out loud—Nurse May, Nurse Day, Nurse Gray—Gray, Ray, they all play their part. Makes me laugh, sort of. I catch my face twisting in the mirror, like I’m chewing something bitter that won’t go away, even when I’m not eating at all.

Most days, I don’t want to talk. The words take too long to come, like wading through soup. I used to enjoy knitting, hymns, visits from my daughter, but now… nothing sticks. I dream at night that John’s feeding me poison cake—ash and salt, that’s all I taste—and I wake up choking. It happens nearly every night. The sadness sits heavy, like a stone in my chest, and it’s been this way—this slow, quiet hurt—almost as long as the voices and suspicions have been with me. Really, the dark mood's been here more than anything else.
D007-D005_h022.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
